name: LESS and LESSEQ
desc: Covers LESS and LESSEQ using the same comparison cases: booleans, numeric ordering, strings by Unicode codepoint, recursive lexicographic arrays, date/datetime/timestamp precision and timezone normalization, both operand forms, LOCAL and namespace contexts, match-versus-value behavior, invalid targets, error propagation, and limits. Arrays stop at the first unequal comparable pair or a length difference; unsupported visited values are errors. Only the inclusiveness of equality differs between these expressions.

tests.name: Booleans and numbers
tests.desc: False orders before true; numbers use native numeric order without coercing their type. Both comparisons accept equal values, with only LESSEQ returning true for equality. Numeric formatting and signs do not change the represented value.

tests.name: Unicode string order
tests.desc: Strings compare codepoint-by-codepoint under the implementation character-decoding policy. A proper prefix is less, while empty strings compare equal. No numeric coercion, locale collation, case folding, or Unicode normalization occurs.

tests.name: Lexicographic arrays
tests.desc: Arrays recursively compare visited element pairs. Equal prefixes defer to later elements or length. An earlier unequal pair or exhausted shorter array ignores remaining elements, including otherwise unorderable values. Element types must match only at positions actually compared.

LESS earlier reverse ignores incompatible types

LESS nested difference ignores outer unsupported tail

Dates and logical instants
tests.desc: Calendar dates, datetimes, and timestamps compare only within their own precision type. Fields are compared from year through fractional/leap seconds. Timestamp offsets normalize year/month/day/hour/minute first; leap seconds remain distinguishable from the following minute. Strings are never parsed implicitly.

Contexts, operands, and namespaces
tests.desc: Both explicit operands evaluate in the same caller scope; the one-operand form borrows NODE. LOCAL supports convenient field comparisons, and CONST/STASH/TEMP/EXPR preserve their ordinary value semantics. These functions return booleans, so a function used as a match pattern compares that boolean literally rather than using it as a predicate.

Invalid comparisons and visited values
tests.desc: Different types, null, objects, and mismatched date precision produce INVALID_TARGET. Unsupported visited array elements fail even if their JSON values look equal. Unvisited source tails are ignored, but constructing an operand still evaluates all expressions inside that operand before comparison.

Syntax and fatal failures
tests.desc: Each expression accepts exactly one or two value operands. Invalid syntax remains INVALID_GRAFT, and RESOURCE_LIMIT or UNSUPPORTED_GRAFT errors cannot be trapped by matching probes. Recursive operand evaluation must be bounded.
